races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Social Symbol
runners_data.spotlight: $60,000 yearling, £145,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; by Violence; sibling to two dirt winners, notably Royal Spa (US 6f-8.5f including 2yo/Grade 2; RPR 116); dam US 5.5f-7f dirt scorer, half-sister to 7f 2yo Grade 1 winner Sippican Harbor; similar to Hidden Gift in terms of sales info; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Sole Ruler
runners_data.spotlight: Inns Of Court half-brother to prolific 5f/7f winner Elegant Erin (including 2yo; RPR 98); dam placed 6f (66), out of 9.4f/1m4f scorer; yard has modest record with 2yos.

runners_data.name: Hidden Gift
runners_data.spotlight: 60,000euros yearling, £150,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; Sioux Nation half-sister to 5f 2yo winner New Theory (RPR 79); dam 7f scorer (72), sister to 6f 2yo Group 3 winner Final Frontier, out of 5f 2yo Listed winner; another interesting newcomer for Wathnan Racing, whose strike-rate with 2yos is strong.

runners_data.name: Dubai Champion
runners_data.spotlight: Modest fourth of six (about 5l behind Fantasy Force) in 5f contest at the York Dante festival, having started the rank outsider; perhaps one for nurseries later on.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Force
runners_data.comment: £56,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; by Persian Force; has precocious signs in his pedigree
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise with third of six in novice contest (5f, good) at the York Dante festival, having attracted a bit of support; the form pick and open to progress to boot.

runners_data.name: Spectacular Diver
runners_data.spotlight: Finished behind a couple of today's rivals at York, failing to back up his Pontefract effort (second of four); effectively needs to prove he's capable of progressing.

runners_data.name: Calef
runners_data.comment: 180,000gns yearling; by Blue Point; the least expensive purchase in the field
runners_data.spotlight: Brings the worst form having trailed home last of four in Carlisle event (5f) won by a smart prospect; achieved little on the figures and needs to improve sharply.

races.name: Book Online At ripon-races.co.uk Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Gone By
runners_data.note: Leading type with class edge, has shown form at this distance on soft going, and benefits from uncontested lead scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Juddmonte Irish Oaks entrant; runner-up to stablemate A La Prochaine (since third in the Cheshire Oaks) on Newbury debut (1m, soft; 17-2) last October, and again forced to settle for second-best on seasonal reappearance at Ascot (1m2f; 10-11 favourite); this is a golden opportunity.

runners_data.name: Golden Step
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was slow away on debut but stays well and represents the main threat to the favourite
runners_data.comment: Sister to an AW winner; it will be interesting to see how she goes in the market
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to the 1m3f AW winner Alfred Spero; slowly away, and only a modest third to a long odds-on favourite on Kempton debut (1m3f fillies' novice; 5-1, RPR 54) four weeks ago; is entitled to have taken on board the lessons learned there, and switches to turf for second start.

runners_data.name: Wootton's Gal
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 313-day layoff with poor debut form, needs significant improvement to feature
runners_data.spotlight: Dam was a 1m4f-1m6f Flat/2m hurdle winner; slowly away and always behind on Thirsk debut (7f maiden fillies', good; 50-1) last July; by far the least likely candidate in this four-runner field.

runners_data.name: Joud
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner stepping up in trip after modest debut, likely to struggle against superior opposition despite longer distance
runners_data.spotlight: 62,000gns foal, and a half-sister to three winners; nothing special, third of four on Newcastle debut (6f novice; 5-1) six months ago; this longer trip should suit on pedigree but she has plenty to find on the limited evidence we've witnessed.

races.paceDynamic: Gone By is the sole confirmed front runner in this four-runner maiden fillies' contest and will control proceedings from the gates without pressure. The other three runners (Golden Step, Wootton's Gal, Joud) are all hold-up types who will settle behind and look to deliver late challenges. Gone By can dictate fractions at her own tempo over this stamina-testing 1m3f trip on soft ground, creating an ideal scenario for the pace-setter. This race shape strongly favours prominent/leading types who can avoid traffic and kick clear before the hold-up brigade can mount their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gone By Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Gone By breaks cleanly and establishes an uncontested lead through steady fractions
scenarios.body: She can quicken off her own pace in the straight while the three hold-up horses struggle to make ground from similar positions. Her superior class and tactical advantage becomes decisive when she finds another gear approaching the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If Gone By goes too slow early or one of the hold-up horses finds unexpected improvement
scenarios.body: Golden Step or another trailer could time their run to perfection and catch the leader tiring in the final 100 yards. The soft ground might just aid a strong-finishing type if Gone By's stamina cracks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Gone By sets overly generous fractions or compounds early
scenarios.body: All four runners converge in a messy finish where positioning and traffic luck determines the outcome. The superior RPR of Gone By still gives her an edge in a desperate finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If Wootton's Gal or Joud has improved dramatically from their poor debuts
scenarios.body: A 313-day break could have worked wonders for Wootton's Gal or Joud might relish this step up in trip. However, their form figures suggest this remains highly unlikely against Gone By's proven class.

watchPoints.text: Gone By's break from the gates - if she misses the start, the entire pace dynamic collapses
Golden Step's early positioning - she was slowly away on debut and cannot afford to spot the leader too much ground
Wootton's Gal's fitness after 313 days off - any market support would indicate hidden improvement from the Fahey stable
The pace through the first half-mile - if Gone By goes too fast she could set it up for the closers
Joud's settling - she needs to relax early to have any chance of staying the extended trip

races.name: Bishopton Equine Handicap

runners_data.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good current form but faces a tactical disadvantage with 13 rivals also coming from behind
runners_data.comment: Ran well in defeat at Thirsk last month and remains well handicapped; one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: She's worked her way back into form and last month's second-place finish at Thirsk (1m, good to firm) was followed by a win at Redcar (1m, good); won on soft ground last September; respected up just 3lb for last time.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Experienced hold-up performer who was desperately unlucky last time but needs significant pace collapse to be effective
runners_data.comment: More encouragement dropped to a Class 5 latest; dangerous mark; place claims
runners_data.spotlight: Just three wins from his 47 starts, the latest back in June 2024; however, he was short-headed off this career-low mark at Hamilton (8.3f, good to firm) last Wednesday and could be in the mix once more; versatile ground-wise.

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with course form but unproven on soft going despite two previous attempts
runners_data.spotlight: Denied a clear run when third over C&D (good) in April and he had the same issue when fourth of 13 at Beverley (8.4f, good to firm) three weeks ago; unproven on slow ground; could be bang there if getting the breaks.

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner to challenge Travis early, giving her a crucial tactical edge in this pace setup
runners_data.comment: On losing run and disappointed last time but her earlier Ayr second brings her into it
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 19 times since winning in December 2024 on her second start; positive signs at the beginning of this campaign but she hasn't backed up those performances on her last two starts; may again be vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Yafaarr
runners_data.note: Hold-up type still seeking first turf win after seven grass attempts, needs everything to fall right
runners_data.comment: 0-6 on turf but kept on well over 7f at Redcar last time; each-way shout up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Newcastle (1m, AW) last October and he's run some good races on turf, but remains winless on grass after seven attempts and needs to produce more than he's managed on turf across his four outings in the spring.

runners_data.name: Superfortress
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced hold-up horse who reared at last start but showed ability when runner-up twice recently
runners_data.comment: Didn't live up to market expectations last time but progress is still a possibility
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't live up to market expectations on handicap debut in April (1m, AW), when he reared at the start, but this very lightly raced 5yo showed what he is capable of when second at Beverley (8.4f, good to firm) three weeks ago, when denied a clear run; unproven on slow ground; on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: The New Bay Pearl
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making stable debut for new trainer after 40-day break, major unknown quantity
runners_data.comment: 0-8 for Roger Varian and well held on recent return for new stable
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who failed to progress for Roger Varian and was soundly beaten at 100-1 on her stable and seasonal debut in April; upset in stalls and withdrawn at Redcar last month (66-1 at the time).

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Recent winner who stays this trip well but must overcome hold-up style disadvantage in this field makeup
runners_data.comment: Three good runs this term, including C&D second and Hamilton win (8.5f); up 2lb; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Knocking on the door prior to winning at Hamilton (8.3f, good) last month and again ran well when third at Redcar (7f, good to firm) nine days ago; also effective on good to soft ground; could be in the shake-up.

runners_data.name: The Childe Of Hale
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 39-day break, won off this mark previously but needs pace to develop
runners_data.spotlight: Won off this mark at Doncaster (7f, good to soft) last July; three lesser runs followed and no return to form on his reappearance in April; he could improve for that latest effort but his claims aren't compelling.

runners_data.name: Havana Touch
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer switching from AW to turf after 34-day gap, unproven in this tactical scenario
runners_data.spotlight: 5yo who was in top form on AW in the spring, with a win at Kempton (1m) being sandwiched by two seconds; showed some promise in May 2024 when he last raced on turf; key player if transferring good form back to grass.

runners_data.name: Avatar Jet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose recent AW form may not translate to this pace-dominated turf contest
runners_data.comment: Stepped forward from his stable debut when winning over C&D 12 days ago; up 4lb; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Made all on AW debut and second start back from a long absence at Southwell (1m, AW) in April, and third there since (1m) in a race that is working out very well; won on turf in 2024 and he's a strong candidate if his good recent form continues back on grass.

runners_data.name: Jesmond Dawn
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from long 117-day layoff, hard to assess current ability
runners_data.spotlight: Below par on his last few starts in the winter but a break may have helped and he's on a handy mark on form as recent as last November; he's capable of running well when fresh and is not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Travis
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner who controls the race but must sustain his effort against 13 rivals tracking behind
runners_data.comment: Front-runner; in good form but his chance probably depends upon an uncontested lead
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who was admirably consistent in the second half of last year and reappeared with a good second at Newcastle in March; however, after a lesser run at Thirsk he was beaten a long way at Redcar only 16 days ago, and needs to leave that latest performance miles behind.

runners_data.name: Eeetee
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 180-day absence, too long away to be confident in current form
runners_data.comment: All six wins have been on turf and he's struggled back on AW of late; plenty to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins at Redcar (1m, good to firm/good to soft) last summer, the latest off today's mark; however, it was a tame end to the season and this 8yo needs to get back on track on his reappearance.

races.paceDynamic: Travis is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner handicap and will dictate terms from the gates, with Donna Nook likely to sit prominent behind him. The remaining 12 runners are all hold-up horses who will need to come from off the pace, creating a compressed field in the rear two-thirds of the pack. With only one pacemaker and no early pressure, Travis can control the tempo and potentially steal a march on the waiting brigade. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those who can get into a position to track the early pace, as the sheer volume of hold-up horses suggests a sprint finish where position will be crucial.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Travis dictates a steady pace without serious early pressure from the prominent runners.
scenarios.body: The lone leader can steal crucial lengths in the straight while the massive field of hold-up horses gets tangled up behind. This benefits Travis himself and any prominent runner like Donna Nook who can secure an ideal tracking position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and the field remains tightly bunched turning for home.
scenarios.body: The 12 hold-up horses get their ideal scenario with a sprint from the furlong pole where the best turn of foot wins. This suits the classier operators who can quicken decisively from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Travis sets unsustainable fractions under pressure from Donna Nook or other forward-placed runners.
scenarios.body: The early leaders weaken badly in the final furlong, allowing the patient hold-up horses to sweep past them. Benefits those with proven finishing kicks who can time their run perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems develop in the large field with runners getting blocked for clear runs.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery where the best-positioned horse wins rather than the best horse on form. Favours those drawn well or ridden by experienced jockeys who can find gaps.

watchPoints.text: Travis must be watched for how much rope he gets in front - if uncontested he could steal an unassailable lead
Donna Nook's early positioning will be crucial as the only prominent runner able to track Travis closely
The draw and early positioning of the 12 hold-up horses will determine who gets the clearest run in the straight
Any early scrimmaging or interference could compromise multiple chances in this tightly-packed field
Jockey changes and stable debuts for The New Bay Pearl and Eeetee make their chances harder to assess

races.name: weatherbysshop.co.uk Handicap

runners_data.name: Raft Up
runners_data.spotlight: Thrived on AW this year, scoring back-to-back at Southwell and Newcastle (both 6f); might have finished closer but for a slow start at Carlisle (6f, good to soft) latest; needs to be fully firing from this joint career-high mark; Liam Wright takes over in saddle.

runners_data.name: Beattie Is Back
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid recent Wolverhampton second and thrives when coming from behind
runners_data.comment: Scored on turf last summer and went close on AW latest but done all his winning over 7f
runners_data.spotlight: 4-29; runner-up off this mark at Wolverhampton (7f; beaten a neck) in February; in rear throughout at York (6f; 40-1) on return from a three-month break; this is slightly easier (Class 5) and Ethan Tindall takes off a handy 5lb.

runners_data.name: Blind Beggar
runners_data.note: Prominent style but poor recent form and questionable effectiveness since stable switch
runners_data.comment: Well held both starts this year and others are much more obvious
runners_data.spotlight: Has won just once since April 2024, at Sandown (5f, good; from 6lb higher) last July; joined this trainer soon after for 15,000gns, and runner-up on stable debut; nowhere near his best in three starts this year, including when twelfth of 20 at York (6f; 50-1) latest.

runners_data.name: Magic Boy
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 211-day break with strong course form but fitness question looms large
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up to an odds-on favourite in a C&D maiden (40-1) last June and mostly competitive since; made the breakthrough in a tight finish at Redcar (7f, Class 5, good; 28-1) last November; 2lb higher for seasonal reappearance, representing an in-form trainer.

runners_data.name: Keldeo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with recent Catterick win but may lack the finishing kick required
runners_data.comment: Has gained all handicap wins at Catterick/Pontefract; makes first visit to Carlisle
runners_data.spotlight: Notched her third Catterick win, fending off Moostar there (6f, good; from 2lb lower) in early April; dropped back to 5f, she has twice finished fourth since, beaten nearly 7l at Carlisle over a fortnight ago; rain would be no major concern, but others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Fortamour
runners_data.note: Six-time course winner who ran well here last month and handles any ground conditions
runners_data.comment: Nearly gained seventh Ripon win latest but his York record isn't anywhere near as strong
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time C&D winner; easing mark and back to form, just held by U Sure Do over C&D (good; 25-1) under four weeks ago; is capable of handling easier ground, and well drawn close to the stands' rail in stall 10; stablemate of William Dewhirst.

runners_data.name: Cairdeas
runners_data.note: Consistent performer over course and distance with solid place record in similar company
runners_data.comment: Done a lot of his racing over 7f and Novello Lad looks his trainer's best shout
runners_data.spotlight: Ex William Haggas; no win since his juvenile days, but has twice ran well over this C&D, including when fourth (from 4lb higher) last August; no match for stablemate Novello Lad at Doncaster (6f, good to soft; 25-1) recently but that comeback run ought to have him spot on for this.

runners_data.name: William Dewhirst
runners_data.note: Struggling to recapture his all-weather form on turf and faces strong pace setup
runners_data.comment: Well treated on best Newcastle AW form and has won over this C&D
runners_data.spotlight: Regular on AW at Newcastle, his last six wins (6f-7f) coming there, most of those under Paul Mulrennan; has struggled to recapture his form in 2026, trailing home ninth of ten at Carlisle (7f, soft; 22-1) 16 days ago; stablemate Fortamour makes way more appeal.

runners_data.name: Bay Breeze
runners_data.note: Course specialist wearing blinkers again after good Hamilton second in headgear last time
runners_data.spotlight: Half of his wins have come over C&D and he finished sixth (Fortamour third) in this race in 2024; runner-up in added blinkers at Hamilton (6f, soft; 11-2) last September, but has failed to sparkle since (0-3); easing mark and a return to Ripon are the positives.

runners_data.name: Men Of Honour
runners_data.note: New to Ruth Carr stable with Irish form but needs to prove turf effectiveness
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish; no surprise were he to need this after seven months off; watch the market
runners_data.spotlight: Formerly with Andrew Slattery, finishing a close fourth to this year's Irish Lincolnshire winner Ribee at Gowran Park (7f, heavy) last October; joined Ruth Carr soon after for 12,000gns; weakened quickly, ninth of 12 to Novello Lad at Doncaster (6f) 18 days ago; now 2lb lower.

runners_data.name: Blazing Son
runners_data.note: Natural leader but much better on all-weather surfaces and returning from 44-day absence
runners_data.comment: Three-time course winner who's had his moments at the stalls; only holds each-way claims
runners_data.spotlight: More productive on AW (5-17) than on turf (2-28) and was only run out of it inside the final furlong at Newcastle (7f Class 5; 9-1) in March; less effective since (0-2) but is slowly easing in the weights, and is perhaps best suited by 6f.

runners_data.name: Glory Hyde
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer who won last time with late surge and suits this strong pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Scored over 5.5f last month and was unlucky over 5f on Tuesday; 6f also suits; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't get the breaks at Beverley (5f, good to firm) on penultimate start, but she pounced late to continue her consistent spell at Redcar (6f, good; from 3lb lower) subsequently, justifying favouritism; is well drawn in stall 12, so should have a positive role to play.

runners_data.name: Miss Willows
runners_data.note: Made all when winning but 54 days off and drops significantly in class from recent efforts
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who won first and last starts in 2025; this season did not start so well
runners_data.spotlight: Made all, scrambling home at Redcar (7f, Class 6, good to soft; from 3lb lower) last September; showed that same speed before weakening on seasonal reappearance at Thirsk (7f, good; 11th of 14; 25-1) in April; has a tricky draw to navigate, unless electing to go far side.

races.paceDynamic: Magic Boy, Blazing Son, and Miss Willows will ensure a strong early gallop over this straight 6f. Magic Boy has shown front-running tendencies and scored at Redcar, while Blazing Son likes to dictate and Miss Willows made all when winning at Redcar last September. Their combined presence guarantees a genuine pace that will test stamina reserves in the closing stages. This sustained gallop clearly favours hold-up horses and those with proven finishing kicks who can capitalize on the inevitable pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Boy and Blazing Son engage early and burn each other out
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop saps the leaders' reserves, creating perfect conditions for closers to sweep past tired front-runners in the final furlong. Hold-up specialists with tactical speed will find gaps as the pace crumbles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Boy or Miss Willows find an uncontested lead and control the fractions
scenarios.body: A single leader manages the pace intelligently, kicking clear before rivals can respond effectively. The winner gets first run and holds on despite late pressure from closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but one prominent runner saves ground and times their move perfectly
scenarios.body: Fortamour or Keldeo track the leaders closely, avoiding the early speed battle but positioning ideally for a well-timed strike. They benefit from the pace without contributing to it, then pounce when the leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Moderate Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the expected pace-setters are restrained or miss the break cleanly
scenarios.body: The race becomes more tactical than anticipated, negating the closing kick advantage and allowing a different type to prevail. Mid-pack runners with versatile styles capitalize on the changed dynamics.

watchPoints.text: Magic Boy's 211-day layoff could see him fold quickly if he takes them along too fast early
Miss Willows and Blazing Son both returning from lengthy breaks may lack the fitness edge needed
William Dewhirst has been poor on turf recently and this strong pace may not suit his style
Glory Hyde's hold-up style perfectly matches the likely pace scenario and she's in top form
Fortamour's course record and recent form make him dangerous if getting the right trip through

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who needs to overcome poor 2024 form but has proven 5f ability on similar going
runners_data.comment: Progressive in lesser company last summer; can have issues at the stalls; needs better
runners_data.spotlight: Won three last year, including at Ayr (5f, good to soft; 13-8 favourite) in July; yet to threaten this year, restless in the stalls at Musselburgh (5f) in April; easing mark - sub 70 for first time in a while - helpful, but tough to recommend at present.

runners_data.name: Wen Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent third at Carlisle but faces tactical disadvantage from rear
runners_data.comment: Placed here (5f); third at Carlisle (5f, good) latest; capable of being competitive.
runners_data.spotlight: Poorly drawn and well beaten on seasonal reappearance here (6f) in April, but much more competitive when third at Carlisle (5f, good; 9-2) 16 days ago; bypassed an option at Catterick on Saturday (unsuitable ground) in favour of this; rain - three wins on soft - would aid his cause.

runners_data.name: High Opinion
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type carrying light weight with claiming rider, likely needs pace collapse
runners_data.comment: Good C&D record and well treated if back to form after four months off
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped as if in need of comeback run at Nottingham (5f, good; sixth of eight) in April; has some decent C&D form to his name and is 10lb lower (and claimer ridden) than when seeing off Our Absent Friends here in August 2024; foolish to discount hastily.

runners_data.name: Speeding Bullet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner resuming after winter break, has course form but low recent profile
runners_data.comment: Form dipped on reappearance but he may rebound with the outing under his belt
runners_data.spotlight: Won off this mark at Pontefract (6f, good; 28-1) last June and finished his season with a pair of second placings at Southwell (6f) and Haydock (5f); low key so far this term, including when seventh (6.5l behind Wen Moon) at Carlisle latest; stablemate of Rock Of England.

runners_data.name: Hurt You Never
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who performed well behind Betweenthesticks at this course recently
runners_data.comment: 14-time winner; showed clear signs of a revival last time; 6lb below last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: 14-66 and somewhat of a Hamilton Park specialist; creditable third to Vince L'Amour (Betweenthesticks second) over C&D on penultimate start but, that aside, she hasn't been overly competitive; easing mark (8lb below her last winning one) offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with recent Musselburgh win, form pick to challenge the pace-setter
runners_data.comment: Has won two of last three and a 5lb penalty shouldn't prevent another bold bid
runners_data.spotlight: Pushed out under hands and heels to score at Musselburgh (5f, good; from 4lb lower) last month, but was no match for stablemate Marajito over C&D (good, 9-2) last week; remains in fine fettle though, and has a C&D win to her name, so she ought to be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 35-day break with decent Newcastle AW form
runners_data.comment: 5f AW win 16 days ago was a good effort; 4lb higher mark demands extra from him
runners_data.spotlight: Resumed winning ways on AW at Newcastle (5f; beating stablemate Herakles) in April; ran well from this revised mark at Pontefract (5f; third, reportedly bled from the nose) subsequently; trainer won this in 2021, 2022, and 2024, so he's one to have on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Front-runner with back-to-back wins this season, perfectly positioned to control pace
runners_data.comment: Two wins, including C&D, and a second from three runs this year; respected despite draw
runners_data.spotlight: Kicked off the season with back-to-back 5f wins at Wolverhampton and Pontefract before being run down by Vince L'Amour over C&D (Hurt You Never third) next time; nowhere near those same levels at Pontefract (ninth of ten) latest, so needs to bounce back.

races.paceDynamic: Betweenthesticks will break smartly and establish an uncontested lead from the rail, with Canaria Queen, Azuinthejungle and Hurt You Never settling in behind but unlikely to pressure early. The prominent runners will track at a comfortable pace while the hold-up horses Wen Moon, High Opinion, Speeding Bullet and Rock Of England drop to the rear. With only one true pace-setter in a small field, Betweenthesticks can dictate fractions and kick for home with energy reserves intact. This tactical setup strongly favours front-running and prominent racers who can secure early position without expending energy in pace battles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Betweenthesticks gets an easy lead and the prominent horses settle kindly behind
scenarios.body: The pace-setter controls the race from pillar to post while the tracking horses have first run on the closers but lack the acceleration to reel in the leader. Betweenthesticks and the prominent runners dominate the finish as the hold-up horses never get into contention.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners get closer to Betweenthesticks than usual and apply pressure from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: Canaria Queen or Azuinthejungle use their recent form advantage to wear down Betweenthesticks in the final furlong. The front-runner's winning run meets stronger opposition than expected while the hold-up horses still struggle to make ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Revival
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes overly sedate and the race turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows Wen Moon and Rock Of England to unleash their finishing kicks over the final 1f. Both have shown ability to quicken when positioned correctly and benefit from the tactical nature of a slowly-run contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Betweenthesticks runs too freely early or the prominent horses crowd the pace unexpectedly
scenarios.body: The anticipated pace advantage disappears and creates a messy, stop-start rhythm that suits no particular running style. High Opinion and Speeding Bullet emerge from the pack as outsiders capitalizing on the tactical confusion ahead of them.

watchPoints.text: Betweenthesticks breaking slowly would completely alter the pace dynamics and leave no clear leader
Canaria Queen and Azuinthejungle getting too close early could create pace pressure that benefits closers
Wen Moon's positioning from the stalls will determine if he can get the strong pace his style requires
High Opinion carrying light weight with inexperienced claimer aboard could cause steering issues
Rock Of England's fitness levels after 35-day absence may show in the final furlong

races.name: Ripon Theatre Festival 5th - 12th July Handicap

runners_data.name: Cobalt Comet
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with place claims based on recent thirds but needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Close third on handicap debut in latest Southwell AW start; switches to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Has posted third-place finishes over 1m at Southwell (AW) and Carlisle (soft) since switched to handicaps; has place claims as things stand and wouldn't need to improve much to open his account.

runners_data.name: Deep Sleep
runners_data.note: Five-race maiden with hold-up style whose best form suggests frame possibilities rather than winning claims
runners_data.comment: Well-held 12th at Thirsk on his return last month; lots more needed on his handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Five-race maiden; best form when fourth on two occasions, including at Hamilton (upped to 1m; handicap debut) latest start; again has frame possibilities but needs progress to get off the mark.

runners_data.name: Karakula Dancer
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with three wins this year but disappointed last time behind Ziggy's Avenger
runners_data.comment: Most consistent since returning in January, including a win over C&D; drawn widest, though
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent record, mostly on AW, this year features three wins; posted a rare unplaced effort last time (behind Ziggy's Avenger) but shaped as if still in form; ran well on turf two starts ago; solid.

runners_data.name: Paroda Diva
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who broke duck last time at 1m on good to soft, suggesting this trip and ground suit
runners_data.comment: 13 races and has won just once (last May) but this first crack at 1m is worth a go
runners_data.spotlight: Proved suited by the step up to 1m at Haydock (good to soft) last time, recording a first win since joining her current yard and belatedly doubling her tally; unexposed at this trip; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Popty Ping
runners_data.note: Only front-runner with decent recent form but 27-day absence could tell in finish after controlling pace
runners_data.comment: Doubled her tally over C&D when winning here in March; respectable effort on turf latest
runners_data.spotlight: Campaigned mostly on AW and overall record is just 1-18, the success in March; however, she continues in form and wasn't disgraced in most recent turf attempt; frame possibilities.

runners_data.name: What Fools Believe
runners_data.note: Hold-up style who won once on AW but failed to back up that form in two subsequent starts
runners_data.comment: Recent Southwell winner but disappointing there last time and looking hard to predict
runners_data.spotlight: Opened her account in 1m AW handicap at Southwell in April; has failed to back up that form in two starts since, latest switched to turf; something to prove.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Avenger
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner showing improvement since gelding operation, keeping-on third last time suggests more to come
runners_data.comment: Hasn't beaten many in three starts, but been gelded; open to improvement on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded prior to showing improvement with keeping-on third at Kempton (1m, AW) on handicap debut last time; may build on that effort and take another step forward; respected off same mark.

runners_data.name: Talking In Kode
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced hold-up filly whose maiden form at Beverley gives her an outside chance in weak contest
runners_data.comment: Likely to be better suited by switching to handicaps soon
runners_data.spotlight: Thrice-raced filly who fared best of the rest behind 2-13 shot in weak maiden at Beverley (7.5f) most recently; that form isn't hugely convincing but it gives her something to possibly build on.

races.paceDynamic: Popty Ping represents the sole confirmed front-runner in this field of eight, meaning she can control the tempo without early pressure from pace rivals. With seven hold-up horses behind her, this sets up a pedestrian early gallop that will gradually build into the straight. The lack of prominent racers means no immediate challenge to Popty Ping's lead, allowing her to dictate fractions and potentially steal a march on closers who may find themselves with too much to do. This tactical scenario strongly favours on-pace types who can sit close to the leader and horses with proven tactical speed to overcome the likely sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Popty Ping faces no early pressure and maintains comfortable fractions
scenarios.body: The pace-setter gets first run in the straight while hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from the back of a small field. Tactical speed and close positioning prove decisive over pure closing ability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too slow and bunches the field entering the final furlong
scenarios.body: Superior class tells in a sprint finish as the best horses find racing room and acceleration. Recent winners and higher-rated performers come to the fore in a cavalry charge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Cracks
scenarios.trigger: If Popty Ping's 27-day break tells and she fades in the final 100 yards
scenarios.body: The long absence shows as early leader weakens, opening the door for hold-up horses with recent runs. Fresh legs and race fitness become the determining factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and creates a blanket finish where anything can happen
scenarios.body: The slow early fractions result in a lottery sprint where lesser-fancied horses with any tactical pace can capitalise. Form gets turned on its head in a messy finale.

watchPoints.text: Popty Ping's 27-day break could see her fade dramatically in the final furlong after setting uncontested fractions
Ziggy's Avenger showed improved form since gelding and could be the main danger if getting a strong finishing run
Watch for early positioning as hold-up horses may struggle to make up ground from the back in a small field
The pace scenario heavily favours Popty Ping if no other horse challenges her early dominance
Paroda Diva's recent 1m win on similar ground makes her the most logical danger to the front-runner
